renders._yaml:
- component: figure
  title: Peak annotation per sample
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample and each segment counts its peaks by the genomic feature HOMER assigned (promoter-TSS, exon, intron, intergenic and so on). It answers where the peaks of each sample land relative to genes.
    How to read: a transcription factor or an active histone mark is expected to concentrate on promoters, while a repressive mark sits mostly in introns and intergenic space. A sample whose split differs from its replicates is worth a check of its quality.
    Lines and annotations: HOMER gives each peak one class by priority, TSS first, then TTS, exons, UTRs, introns and intergenic. The promoter-TSS window is from 1 kb upstream to 100 bp downstream of the start site, HOMER's default.
    Source: http://homer.ucsd.edu/homer/ngs/annotation.html
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    color: annotation_class
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      annotation_class: Genomic feature
      count: Peaks

- component: figure
  title: Distance to nearest TSS
  description: |-
    Each bar counts peaks in a bin of their signed distance to the nearest transcription start site, split by genomic feature. It answers how close the peaks sit to promoters.
    How to read: a tall bar around zero means promoter-bound peaks. A broad, flat distribution with long tails means the signal is mostly distal. Negative values are upstream of the start site and positive values downstream.
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: distance_to_tss
    color: annotation_class
    labels:
      distance_to_tss: Distance to nearest TSS (bp)
      annotation_class: Genomic feature

- component: card
  title: Annotated peaks
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of annotated peaks, and the bars rank the feature classes that hold most of them. The secondary number is the count of chromosomes the peaks fall on. It answers how many peaks there are and where they land.
    How to read: a class that dominates the ranking tells what kind of region the signal marks. Open the annotation bars to compare samples.
  column: chr
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: annotation_class
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: peaks, by feature class

- component: card
  title: Peaks by feature class
  description: |-
    Each unit is one annotated peak and the ring splits them by the genomic feature HOMER assigned. It answers what share of peaks sit in promoters, exons, introns or intergenic regions.
    How to read: compare the promoter share with what is expected for the mark or factor. HOMER assigns one class per peak by priority, TSS first and intergenic last.
    Source: http://homer.ucsd.edu/homer/ngs/annotation.html
  column: annotation_class
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: annotation_class
  caption: peaks, by feature class
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Genes with a peak
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct genes that are the nearest promoter of a peak, and the bars rank the feature classes by how many genes they reach. It answers how many genes the peaks can regulate.
    How to read: HOMER assigns the nearest start site whatever the distance, so a distal peak still names a gene. Filter to the promoter class for the confident targets.
  column: gene_name
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: annotation_class
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: genes, by feature class

- component: card
  title: Peak score
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median peak score, with a box for the quartiles. It answers how strong the typical peak is.
    How to read: the score comes from the peak caller, not from HOMER, so compare it between samples called the same way. A sample with a much lower median has weaker enrichment.
  column: peak_score
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Annotated peaks table
  description: |-
    Each row is a peak with its position, score, feature class, distance to the nearest start site and gene. It answers which peaks and genes to follow up and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by score, and filter by feature class to keep promoter peaks.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: peak_id

- component: card
  title: Peak score distribution
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest peak score, and the histogram shows how scores are spread over all peaks. It answers how many peaks are strong and how many are weak.
    How to read: most callers give many weak peaks and a long tail of strong ones. A distribution with no tail means little enrichment over background.
  column: peak_score
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - q3
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: top score, with the typical peak

- component: advanced_viz
  id: tss_distance
  title: Peak distribution around the TSS
  description: |-
    Each curve is a sample: the fraction of its peaks that fall in each bin of distance to the nearest transcription start site, 250 bp wide as set by this catalog's recipe. It answers whether the peaks concentrate at promoters.
    How to read: a sharp spike at zero means promoter-bound signal, as for an active mark or a promoter-binding factor. A flat curve means the peaks sit across gene bodies and intergenic space. Curves that differ between replicates point to a quality problem.
    Lines and annotations: the vertical marker is the start site at zero. The shaded band runs from 1 kb upstream to 100 bp downstream of it, the window HOMER uses to call a peak promoter-TSS by default.
    Source: http://homer.ucsd.edu/homer/ngs/annotation.html
  kind: profile
  config:
    reference_x: 0
    reference_label: TSS
    shaded_bands:
    - - -1000
      - 100
      - Promoter-TSS window
    x_title: Distance to nearest TSS (bp)
    y_title: Fraction of peaks
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: distance_to_tss
    y: fraction

- component: figure
  title: Peak distribution around the nearest TSS
  description: |-
    Each line is a sample: the fraction of its peaks in each 250 bp bin around the nearest transcription start site. It answers how the peak positions of the samples compare on the same axis.
    How to read: lines that overlay each other mean consistent peak positions. A sample with a lower central peak has more distal signal than the others.
  visu_type: line
  dict_kwargs:
    x: distance_to_tss
    y: fraction
    color: sample
    labels:
      distance_to_tss: Distance to nearest TSS (bp)
      fraction: Fraction of peaks
      sample: Sample

- component: card
  title: Peaks in the window
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of peaks counted in the 20 kb window around the start sites, and the histogram shows how many peaks each bin holds. It answers how many peaks fall near a gene.
    How to read: a distribution with one huge bin and many near-empty ones is the signature of promoter signal. An even spread means peaks are not tied to start sites.
  column: peak_count
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: total, with the busiest bin

- component: card
  title: Share of peaks per bin
  description: |-
    The hero number is the largest share of a sample's peaks in a single bin, and the histogram shows how the shares are spread over bins. It answers how concentrated the peaks are.
    How to read: a large maximum with a median near zero means the peaks pile up at one distance, usually the start site. A small maximum means they are spread out.
  column: fraction
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - q3
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: top bin, with the typical bin

- component: card
  title: Peaks per sample
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of peaks in the window and the bar shows each sample's share of it. It answers whether the samples contribute evenly.
    How to read: a sample with a very small share has fewer peaks and its profile is less reliable.
  column: peak_count
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: sample
  caption: peaks, by sample

- component: table
  title: Distance profile table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample and a distance bin with its peak count and the fraction of that sample's peaks. It answers exactly how many peaks sit at each distance.
    How to read: sort by peak count to find the dominant bin of each sample.
